name: Confirm that what the books say was received matches what the bank and gateway actually received
priorityReason: Without it the school knows what it recorded but not what it holds, and the two drift apart silently.

goal.capability: to check every recorded movement against the bank and gateway statements
goal.outcome: the books and the bank agree, and every difference has been found and explained rather than left to accumulate

businessRules.rule: Reconciliation confirms that what the books say was received matches what was actually received. It never adjusts the books to match the statement; a difference is explained or corrected at source.

Checking happens twice. Each entry is checked as it is recorded — a gateway payment against the gateway record, a physical payment against the bank using the returned challan copy before the data is entered from it — and again across the whole month.
Statements are imported rather than keyed wherever the format allows. A statement typed by hand is a second place for an error to enter.
The monthly reconciliation covers every movement, not fees alone. Salaries, expenses and refunds all pass through the same account and all have to be matched.
A match may be undone. A wrongly matched line is worse than an unmatched one, because it hides a difference rather than showing it.
An unmatched item at sign-off carries what was done about it and a written note. Nothing is left unexplained simply because the period closed.
Where the record was wrong rather than the statement, a correction is raised through the payment correction route rather than adjusted here.

A statement line with no recorded movement, and a recorded movement with no statement line, are both reported. The second is how a payment recorded but never received is found, which is the whole point of the exercise.
The difference between the books and the statement is itemised line by line. It is never forced to zero by an adjusting entry nobody can explain.
The School Admin signs off, not the person who performed the reconciliation. Somebody checking their own work is not a control.
The opening balance is carried from the previous signed-off reconciliation, and unresolved differences carry forward with it. A period cannot be reconciled in isolation.
A signed-off reconciliation is not reopened. A later discovery is handled in the current period, since reopening a signed period changes a figure somebody has already relied on.

transitions.condition: Every line on both sides is matched.
Items remain unmatched after the matching run.
Every difference is resolved or explained (BR-6).
Signed off with the remaining differences carried forward and noted (BR-6, BR-11).

basicFlow.userAction: Checks each entry against its source as it is recorded — the gateway record for an online payment, or the bank and the returned challan copy for a physical one.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Flags a payment whose source cannot be confirmed before the data is entered from it.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Finance → Reconciliation periods → Start reconciliation
basicFlow.userAction: Starts the reconciliation for the account and period at month end.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Carries the opening balance from the previous signed-off reconciliation and lists every movement in the period.

basicFlow.userAction: Imports the bank and gateway statements for the period.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Reads the statement lines rather than having them keyed, and reports any line it could not read.
Matches statement lines against recorded movements on reference, amount and date, and lists what is unmatched on either side.

basicFlow.userAction: Investigates each difference and matches what can be matched by hand.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the match and who made it. A match can be undone if it turns out to be wrong.

basicFlow.navigation: Unmatched items → Raise correction, or Carry forward
basicFlow.userAction: Raises a correction where the record was wrong, or carries the item forward as timing with a written note.
basicFlow.function: raisePaymentCorrection(paymentId, type, description) or carryForward(itemId, note)
basicFlow.systemResponse: Requires an action and a note for anything not matched.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Finance → Reconciliation periods → Sign off
basicFlow.userAction: Reviews the reconciliation and signs it off.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the sign-off, closes the period and carries any unresolved difference forward.

alternateFlows.condition: A statement line has no recorded movement
alternateFlows.behaviour: Money reached the bank that the books do not show. It is investigated and recorded, since unrecorded income is as much a problem as a missing payment (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: A recorded movement has no statement line
alternateFlows.behaviour: The books show money the bank never received. This is how a payment recorded but never made is found, and it is the reason the exercise exists (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: The record was wrong rather than the statement
alternateFlows.behaviour: A payment correction is raised rather than the reconciliation being adjusted, and the corrected entry is picked up here afterwards (BR-7).

alternateFlows.condition: A cheque was issued in the period but cleared in the next
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is carried forward as timing with a note. Timing differences are normal; unexplained ones are not (BR-6).

alternateFlows.condition: A line was matched to the wrong movement
alternateFlows.behaviour: The match is undone. A wrongly matched line hides a difference rather than showing it, which is worse than leaving it unmatched (BR-5).
The reconciliation is signed off with each remaining difference carried forward and noted, rather than the period being held open indefinitely (BR-6, BR-11).

exceptions.condition: The statement file cannot be read
exceptions.systemResponse: Nothing is imported and the format expected is named.
exceptions.messageShown: This file could not be read. Import a CSV in the format the bank provides.

exceptions.condition: The statement covers a different period from the reconciliation
exceptions.messageShown: This statement covers August. The reconciliation is for September.

exceptions.condition: Two movements match one statement line equally well
exceptions.systemResponse: Neither is matched automatically and both are offered for a manual decision.
exceptions.messageShown: Two payments of PKR 4,000 on the same date match this line. Choose which.

exceptions.condition: An item is left unmatched with no action or note
exceptions.systemResponse: The reconciliation cannot be signed off (BR-6).
exceptions.messageShown: 3 items have no explanation. Record what was done about each before signing off.

exceptions.condition: Accounts attempt to sign off their own reconciliation
exceptions.messageShown: Only a School Admin can sign off a reconciliation.

exceptions.condition: The previous period has not been signed off
exceptions.systemResponse: The reconciliation cannot start, since the opening balance is not settled (BR-11).
exceptions.messageShown: August has not been signed off. Complete it before starting September.
September was signed off on 08-10-2026. Handle the difference in the current period.
The difference of PKR 4,000 is not explained line by line. It cannot be signed off.

exceptions.condition: A payment's source cannot be confirmed at entry
exceptions.systemResponse: It is flagged rather than entered as verified, so the month end finds it.
exceptions.messageShown: This payment could not be confirmed against the bank. It is flagged for reconciliation.

openQuestions.question: In what format does the school's bank provide statements, and can they be imported at all?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and if they cannot be imported every line is keyed by hand.

openQuestions.question: How long may a difference remain unresolved before it must be escalated?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. At present an item can be carried forward indefinitely.

openQuestions.question: Should reconciliation cover cash held at the office as well as bank and gateway?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and a cash drawer is where a shortfall is most easily hidden.

openQuestions.question: Who reconciles when the same person records payments and performs the reconciliation in a small office?
openQuestions.assumption: Sign-off by School Admin is the control, but a very small office may have neither.

openQuestions.question: What is the financial year the reconciliation periods run against?
openQuestions.assumption: Not defined anywhere in the feature document.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: bulk-actions
conventionsApplied.rule: Any bulk operation reports a per-row result, commits valid rows and lists rejected rows with the reason. A bulk action never fails as a whole because of one bad row.

conventionsApplied.name: attachments
conventionsApplied.rule: Uploaded files are limited to 10 MB and to PDF, JPG, PNG, DOCX and XLSX unless a use case states otherwise. File type is validated by content, not by extension.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
